blocks.text: Transport and communication: the arteries of the economy

Transport moves goods and people from one place to another; communication moves information. Together they join producers to markets, link regions, and help national unity. A well-developed network of transport and communication is a sign, and also a cause, of economic development. A country such as India, with its size and diversity, depends on all four main modes: roads, railways, waterways and airways, supported by pipelines and a growing system of communication networking.
The area from which a port draws its exports and to which it sends its imports; the region served by the port through its road, rail and river links.
Roads

Roads are the most used mode of transport in India for short and medium distances. They are cheaper to build than railways, can cross difficult terrain such as hills, give **door-to-door service**, and reach villages that rail does not. Roads are classified by the authority that builds and maintains them.

blocks.caption: Classes of roads in India (as per NCERT)
rows: Connect extreme parts of the country, state capitals and ports; built and maintained by the central government
Golden Quadrilateral; North-South and East-West corridors
Join state capitals to district headquarters and important towns; maintained by the states
Link district headquarters with other places in the district
Connect villages to nearby towns; promoted under the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana
Built by the Border Roads Organisation (formed 1960) in remote border areas
Roads in the Himalayas and the desert border

blocks.text: The **Golden Quadrilateral Super Expressway** joins the four metropolitan cities, Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata, with a high-speed multi-lane road. The **North-South corridor** connects Srinagar in the north with Kanyakumari in the south, and the **East-West corridor** connects Silchar in the east with Porbandar in the west. The Nagpur Plan of 1943 was an early plan for road development. Roads have drawbacks: they are less suitable for bulky heavy goods over very long distances, and road accidents and congestion are serious problems.
Railways

The railway is the principal mode for long-distance passenger and freight traffic, and it carries bulk goods such as coal, ores, cement and food grains cheaply. The first passenger train ran in 1853 from Mumbai (Bori Bunder) to Thane, a distance of 34 km. The Indian Railways network is organised into zones. The track uses three gauges (distance between the rails): **broad gauge** (1.676 m), **metre gauge** (1.000 m) and **narrow gauge** (0.762 m and 0.610 m); the programme of gauge conversion is replacing the others by broad gauge. The Konkan Railway, built along the west coast in the 1990s, is an engineering achievement because it crosses many rivers and hills.
Waterways and pipelines

Waterways are the cheapest means of transport for heavy, bulky goods and consume less fuel, but they are slow and depend on the depth of water. India has navigable rivers and canals, and the Inland Waterways Authority of India was set up in 1986. Three waterways have been declared **National Waterways**: **NW-1** on the Ganga from Allahabad to Haldia (1,620 km); **NW-2** on the Brahmaputra from Sadiya to Dhubri (891 km); and **NW-3** on the West Coast Canal in Kerala from Kottapuram to Kollam (205 km).

**Oil and gas pipelines** move crude oil, petroleum products and natural gas over long distances. They need a high initial cost but have a very low running cost, little loss and no handling at intermediate points, and they are safe and continuous. Important lines include the oil pipeline from Naharkatia in Assam through Guwahati to Barauni in Bihar, the Salaya to Mathura line, and the **HBJ (Hazira-Bijaipur-Jagdishpur) gas pipeline**. Their disadvantage is that the route is fixed and a leak or breakage is hard to repair.
Airways

Air transport is the fastest mode, and it is the only practical link to remote and hilly regions such as the North-East and Jammu and Kashmir. It is also used for high-value, urgent and perishable goods. It is also the costliest mode, and it depends on weather. Air India, formed in the early 1950s after the nationalisation of airlines, and later other carriers, serve domestic and international routes, while international airports at the metropolitan cities connect India to the world.

blocks.problem: A train covers a route of 1,260 km at an average speed of 60 km per hour. After track improvement, its average speed becomes 70 km per hour. How much time is saved?
blocks.solution: Time = distance / speed. Earlier time = 1260/60 = 21 hours. New time = 1260/70 = 18 hours. Time saved = 21 - 18 = 3 hours. A rise in speed gives a saving that is proportionally smaller than the percentage rise in speed, because time varies inversely with speed.

blocks.text: Communication networking

Communication has moved from the post and the telegraph to electronic systems. **Radio** and **television** give mass communication and reach rural areas; All India Radio and Doordarshan are the national public broadcasters. **Satellite communication** through the INSAT system provides telephone, television, weather and disaster-warning services, and it covers remote areas without cables. The **internet** links computers worldwide, supporting e-mail, e-commerce, online banking and education. Mobile telephony and broadband have made information available quickly and at low cost, and the spread of communication has also created jobs in the information sector.
International trade: changing pattern of India's foreign trade

The exchange of goods and services between countries. The difference between the value of exports and imports is the balance of trade. If imports are larger it is a trade deficit, and if exports are larger it is a trade surplus.

Trade is based on differences in resources, climate, skills and technology, so countries trade to obtain what they cannot produce, or cannot produce cheaply. The **pattern of India's foreign trade has changed**. In the early decades after independence, agricultural goods and raw materials such as tea, jute products and cotton textiles dominated exports. Later, engineering goods, gems and jewellery, chemicals, and petroleum products grew in importance, and then information-technology services. The import side is dominated by petroleum and crude oil, machinery, fertilisers, edible oils, and gold and precious stones, since India lacks enough crude oil. Over time the country has moved from exporting mainly primary goods to exporting more manufactured goods and services. Figures change from year to year, so as per NCERT it is the direction of change that matters.

blocks.problem: In a year, a country exports goods worth 540 units and imports goods worth 720 units. Find the balance of trade and express the deficit as a percentage of imports.
blocks.solution: Balance of trade = exports - imports = 540 - 720 = -180 units, which is a deficit of 180 units. As a percentage of imports, deficit = 180/720 x 100 = 25 per cent. The negative sign means the country buys more than it sells abroad and must meet the gap through other earnings such as services or capital inflows.
blocks.answer: Deficit of 180 units, which is 25 per cent of imports

blocks.text: Seaports, their hinterland, and airports

About 95 per cent of India's trade by volume moves by sea, so seaports are the gateways of foreign trade, as per NCERT. A port's success depends on its **hinterland** and on the depth and shelter of its harbour. On the west coast the major ports include **Kandla**, **Mumbai**, **Jawaharlal Nehru Port (Nhava Sheva)**, **Marmagao**, **New Mangalore** and **Kochi**. On the east coast they include **Tuticorin**, **Chennai**, **Visakhapatnam**, **Paradip** and **Kolkata (with Haldia)**. Kandla in Gujarat is a tidal port, developed after independence to replace the loss of Karachi. Jawaharlal Nehru Port was developed to relieve congestion at Mumbai, and it is a leading container port. Visakhapatnam is a landlocked and well-protected harbour with great depth. Kolkata is a riverine port on the Hugli, and Haldia was built to ease its silting problem.

**Airports** serve as air gateways, mainly for high-value, light and perishable cargo and for passengers. The international airports at metropolitan cities such as Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata handle most international passenger and cargo traffic.

Quick revision: Roads give door-to-door service; railways suit bulk and long distance; waterways are cheapest but slow; airways are fastest but costliest; pipelines have high set-up cost and low running cost. NW-1 is Allahabad-Haldia, NW-2 is Sadiya-Dhubri, NW-3 is Kottapuram-Kollam. Broad gauge is 1.676 m. Trade pattern has shifted from primary goods towards manufactures and services.

Common mistakes: (1) Mixing the golden quadrilateral (four metros) with the North-South and East-West corridors. (2) Saying that waterways are fast; they are cheap, not fast. (3) Treating trade balance as profit; it is only exports minus imports. (4) Using the wrong gauge value. (5) Quoting exact trade statistics from memory, which change with time. In the exam, use the qualitative pattern and the facts given in the question stem.

questions.stem: The Golden Quadrilateral Super Expressway connects which four cities?
questions.explanation: The Golden Quadrilateral is a high-speed road joining the four metropolitan cities Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata. The Srinagar-Kanyakumari road is the North-South corridor and Silchar-Porbandar is the East-West corridor.

optionRationale.1: Jaipur and Ahmedabad are not among the four corners of the quadrilateral.
optionRationale.2: Srinagar and Kanyakumari are the ends of the North-South corridor.
optionRationale.4: Silchar and Porbandar are the ends of the East-West corridor.

questions.objective: Identify the cities joined by the Golden Quadrilateral

questions.stem: National Waterway No. 1 (NW-1) runs along the
options: West Coast Canal from Kottapuram to Kollam
questions.explanation: NW-1 is the Ganga waterway from Allahabad to Haldia, about 1,620 km long. NW-2 is on the Brahmaputra from Sadiya to Dhubri and NW-3 is the West Coast Canal in Kerala from Kottapuram to Kollam.

optionRationale.4: The Godavari is not declared as NW-1.

questions.stem: Which Indian port is a tidal port, developed after independence in Gujarat to meet the loss of Karachi?
questions.explanation: Kandla in the Gulf of Kachchh is a tidal port, developed after independence to handle the trade that earlier went through Karachi, which went to Pakistan. Marmagao is in Goa, Paradip is in Odisha and Chennai is on the east coast.

optionRationale.1: Marmagao is in Goa and is not a tidal port.
optionRationale.3: Paradip is in Odisha on the east coast.
optionRationale.4: Chennai is an artificial harbour on the east coast.

questions.objective: Identify Kandla as a tidal port

questions.stem: The distance between the rails in broad gauge in India is
questions.explanation: Broad gauge in India is 1.676 m between the rails. Metre gauge is 1.000 m and narrow gauge is 0.762 m (and 0.610 m in some lines). A 2.000 m gauge is not used.

optionRationale.3: 2.000 m is not a gauge used by Indian Railways.

questions.stem: Match the Indian port in List-I with its feature in List-II.
questions.explanation: Kandla is a tidal port, Visakhapatnam is a landlocked well-protected deep harbour, Jawaharlal Nehru Port is a major container port, and Kolkata is a riverine port on the Hugli. That gives A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV.

optionRationale.1: This swaps the features of Kandla and Visakhapatnam.
optionRationale.3: This assigns the container feature to Kandla and the riverine feature to Visakhapatnam.
optionRationale.4: This reverses the correct matching almost completely.

right: IV. Riverine port on the Hugli

questions.stem: A country exports goods worth 540 units and imports goods worth 720 units in a year. Its trade deficit as a percentage of imports is
questions.explanation: Trade deficit = imports - exports = 720 - 540 = 180 units. As a percentage of imports, 180/720 x 100 = 25 per cent. Taking the deficit over exports gives 33.3 per cent, which is not what the question asks, and 75 per cent is the ratio of exports to imports.

optionRationale.1: 20 per cent does not follow from 180/720.
optionRationale.2: 33.3 per cent uses exports (540) as the base instead of imports.
optionRationale.4: 75 per cent is exports as a share of imports, not the deficit share.

questions.objective: Calculate the trade balance and its share

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Roads are the most widely used mode of transport in India for short and medium distances.
Reason (R): Roads provide door-to-door service and can reach villages and hilly areas where railways cannot.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Road transport is cheaper to build, can be built in difficult terrain and gives door-to-door delivery, which is why it is so widely used over short and medium distances. The reason therefore correctly explains the assertion.

optionRationale.2: The reason does directly explain the assertion, so it is more than a related fact.
optionRationale.3: The assertion is true, so this option is wrong.
optionRationale.4: The assertion is true and not false.

questions.objective: Explain why roads are widely used

questions.stem:
Consider the statements.
A. NW-1 runs on the Ganga from Allahabad to Haldia.
B. NW-2 runs on the Brahmaputra from Sadiya to Dhubri.
C. NW-3 runs on the Godavari in Andhra Pradesh.
Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: NW-1 on the Ganga and NW-2 on the Brahmaputra are described correctly. NW-3 is the West Coast Canal in Kerala from Kottapuram to Kollam and not on the Godavari, so statement C is false.

optionRationale.1: B is also correct, so A alone is incomplete.
optionRationale.2: A is also correct, so B alone is incomplete.
optionRationale.3: C is false, so this pair cannot be correct.

questions.stem: Which communication system in India provides telephone, television, weather and disaster-warning services across remote areas through space?
questions.explanation: INSAT is the Indian National Satellite system, a multipurpose system supplying telecommunication, broadcasting, meteorological and search and rescue services. The telegraph, wired telephone and postal network depend on cables or physical delivery.

optionRationale.1: The telegraph used wires and has no weather services.
optionRationale.3: Wired lines cannot cover remote areas easily.
optionRationale.4: The postal system is a physical delivery service.

questions.objective: Identify the role of satellite communication

questions.stem: A train covers 1,260 km at an average speed of 60 km per hour. If its average speed rises to 70 km per hour, how much time will it save on the journey?
questions.explanation: Original time = 1260/60 = 21 hours and the new time = 1260/70 = 18 hours. The saving is 21 - 18 = 3 hours. Journey time depends inversely on speed, so a rise in speed gives a saving smaller in proportion than the rise itself.

optionRationale.1: 1 hour is too small a saving.
optionRationale.2: 2 hours is too small a saving.
optionRationale.4: 4 hours is more than the computed saving.

questions.objective: Compute time saved from a change in speed

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Waterways are the cheapest mode for transporting heavy and bulky goods.
Reason (R): Waterways are the fastest mode of transport.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: The assertion is true: inland water transport and sea transport carry bulky goods at a low cost per tonne-kilometre and use less fuel. The reason is false, since waterways are slow, and air transport is the fastest mode.

optionRationale.1: The reason is false, so it cannot be a correct explanation.
optionRationale.2: The reason is false, so both cannot be true.
optionRationale.4: The assertion is true, so it cannot be false with a true reason.

questions.stem: The cost of carrying goods is 2.5 monetary units per tonne-km by road and 1.2 units per tonne-km by rail. To carry 500 tonnes over 800 km, how much more does the road cost than the rail?
questions.explanation: Tonne-km = 500 x 800 = 400,000. Road cost = 2.5 x 400,000 = 1,000,000 units and rail cost = 1.2 x 400,000 = 480,000 units. The difference = 1,000,000 - 480,000 = 520,000 units, so the road is dearer by that amount.

optionRationale.2: 480,000 is the cost by rail alone.
optionRationale.3: 1,000,000 is the cost by road alone.
optionRationale.4: 320,000 does not result from the data.

questions.objective: Compare transport costs over a given distance

questions.stem:
Consider the statements on India's foreign trade.
A. Exports earlier consisted mainly of agricultural goods and raw materials.
B. The share of manufactured goods and services in exports has grown over time.
C. Petroleum and crude oil form a large part of imports.
D. India has a permanent trade surplus.
Which are correct?
questions.explanation: Early exports were mostly agricultural and raw materials, manufactures and services have grown in importance, and petroleum is a large import because India lacks enough crude oil. D is false, since India often has a trade deficit.

optionRationale.1: D is false, so this pair cannot be right.
optionRationale.2: A is also correct, so B and C alone is incomplete.
optionRationale.3: D is false and A is true, so this pair is wrong.

questions.objective: Evaluate the changing pattern of India's trade

questions.stem: Why is air transport used for fresh flowers, fruits and medicines even though it is costly?
options: Because air transport has the lowest cost per tonne-km
Because these goods are perishable or urgent and speed saves value
Because airports are always closer to farms
Because air routes are never affected by weather
questions.explanation: Air transport is the fastest mode, and for perishable, light and high-value goods the time saved prevents spoilage or meets urgent demand, so the higher cost is acceptable. Air transport is the costliest, not the cheapest, and it is affected by weather.

optionRationale.1: Air transport is the costliest mode per tonne-km.
optionRationale.3: Airports are not always close to farms.
optionRationale.4: Air transport is affected by weather, such as fog and storms.

questions.objective: Reason out the use of air transport

questions.stem: Which pair of the road corridors with the places they connect is correct?
questions.explanation: The North-South corridor joins Srinagar in the north to Kanyakumari in the south. The East-West corridor joins Silchar in the east to Porbandar in the west. The other pairs interchange these terminals.

optionRationale.2: Silchar and Porbandar join the East-West corridor.
optionRationale.3: Srinagar and Kanyakumari join the North-South corridor.
optionRationale.4: Delhi and Chennai are corners of the Golden Quadrilateral and not of the East-West corridor.

questions.objective: Differentiate the corridors of the highway network
